A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The supplied v1 ends after the references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes supplementary Sections A-C. The comparison covers all material actually supplied.

before.justification: v1 reports original SkyReels-Text results on poster editing, AnyText, IAM and CVL, together with font-reference and loss-weight ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports OCR evaluations, user preferences, dataset analyses and further editing demonstrations.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds a paragraph-editing adaptation through continued LoRA training on 10K paragraph samples. The core dual-stream conditioning, weighted loss and eight-step distillation remain unchanged. Newly specified Nano Banana and SAM2 usage documents implementation details without establishing replacements to the original method.

E1.justification: The existing editing and handwriting benchmarks remain. v2 adds reported OCR detection/recognition evaluation on regular and non-regular fonts, small-text and garbled-text editing scenarios, and paragraph-level training and evaluation. These substantially broaden the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: Calligrapher is added to both existing editing comparisons in Tables 1 and 2. The new OCR comparison in Table 6 evaluates PP-OCRv4, PP-OCRv5, PaddleOCR-VL, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct against the proposed OCR model, substantially expanding evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New designs include a randomly held-out 200-image OCR benchmark with regular/non-regular evaluations, a win/tie/loss preference study, and paragraph adaptation using 5K curated plus 5K synthetic samples. Section 3.2 also changes the stated filtering rule from small or overlapping regions to overlapping regions. These additions do not establish reruns of the retained benchmarks.

E4.justification: The original font-reference and loss-weight ablations remain unchanged. v2 adds dataset validation through style-feature t-SNE, NED/DINO distributions, text-length and character-overlap analyses, plus targeted small-text and paragraph-editing case studies. These directly examine data quality, decoupling and applicability beyond the original analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental uncertainty estimates. v2's dataset histograms and preference percentages describe observations rather than uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: All pre-existing numerical rows in Tables 1-4 are unchanged. Substantial new results include Calligrapher scores, OCR performance such as 0.9276 non-regular-font sentence accuracy, and preference wins such as 84.5% against FLUX-Kontext-Pro. Dataset diagnostics and additional qualitative editing results further expand the evidence; these are newly reported outcomes, not improvements to retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix B introduces a limited quantitative definition of Effective Text: replacements with less than 20% character overlap with the original. The latent-concatenation and weighted-loss equations remain equivalent, and no new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction promotes the already-described content-style decoupling pipeline and its 100K image pairs to an explicit fourth contribution. The central claims about reference-guided font control, simultaneous regional editing, zero-shot transfer and state-of-the-art performance remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for background mixing and random cropping, and argues that content divergence matters more than semantic alignment in style references. Appendix C explicitly identifies dense artistic paragraph generation as difficult because suitable training data are scarce. The original ablation interpretations remain intact.

D1.justification: Appendices A-B substantially expand reproducibility information: OCR data sources, expert annotation, filtering thresholds, Nano Banana editing, SAM2 segmentation, background blending, random cropping, and NED/DINO acceptance thresholds of 0.9/0.8. v2 also identifies benchmark OCR evaluators, reports approximately eight-second inference on an A800, and supplies a code/model access link. Much of this is newly disclosed detail, not demonstrated procedural change.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Calligrapher, Qwen3-VL, SAM2, DuGuangOCR, MUSIQ, NRQM and Q-Align, mainly supporting comparisons and implementation documentation. The related-work argument remains largely unchanged. Consolidating duplicate Seedream references and updating publication metadata do not represent removal or addition of distinct research.

P1.justification: The main section order and narrative are retained. v2 polishes grammar and terminology, revises portions of the experimental discussion and conclusion, expands the contribution list, and organizes additional explanations into supplementary Sections A-C.

P2.justification: v2 adds a data-pipeline diagram, preference chart, OCR and dataset displays, editing galleries, and Tables 5-8. Tables 1-2 gain comparator rows and several existing displays move. v1 Figure 2 reappears as v2 Figure 14, while the architecture diagram and original qualitative comparisons are retained with presentation refinements.

improvement.justification: Appendices A-B substantially address an important weakness of v1: its OCR contribution and data-quality claims lacked direct evaluation and detailed curation documentation. v2 adds comparative OCR evidence, dataset diagnostics and concrete reproduction details, while broader comparisons and an explicit paragraph-editing limitation strengthen assessment of applicability. The user study lacks participant counts, sample counts and uncertainty estimates, limiting that addition's evidential value, but the overall gains in validation and transparency are substantial.
